chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
"When the sun sets, iftar becomes permissible and the salat becomes obligatory. When you have performed the Maghrib prayer, then the time of the later night prayer has entered, until midnight.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat due at sunset
key_terms.الْإِفْطَارُ: breaking the fast at the proper time
key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the Maghrib prayer performed after sunset
key_terms.اِنْتِصَافِ اللَّيْلِ: midnight, the endpoint mentioned for this prayer time
key_terms.غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun has set; the onset of sunset time

ai.seo_question: When does it become permissible to break the fast, and when does the time of 'Isha begin?
ai.summary: This hadith states that sunset marks the permissibility of breaking the sawm and the obligation of Maghrib salat. It also establishes that after performing Maghrib, the time for the 'Isha prayer begins and lasts until midnight.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.663 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When the sun sets, it becomes permissible to break the fast (if one is fasting) and the Maghrib prayer becomes obligatory. Once you have performed the Maghrib prayer, the time for the Isha (night) prayer begins and extends until midnight."
